title: Checkpoint 12: Hans vs Stockfish (skill 0)
notes: Checkpoint after game 12, from the Italian Game: Hans plays the yardstick, Stockfish at skill 0. Nothing is studied afterwards.

moves.thought: This is the Giuoco Piano, and with my pawn already on c3 the natural plan is to build the big center immediately with d4. After 5.d4 exd4 6.cxd4 Bb4+ 7.Nc3 I get strong central control, and I avoided tempting but bad tries like Bxf7+ or Nxe5 which just lose material after Kxf7 or Nxe5.

Black's 5...Bb6 leaves the e5 pawn loose, so I grab it: 6.dxe5 Nxe5 runs into 7.Nxe5 Nxe5 8.Bxf7+ Kxf7 9.Qd5+ winning back the piece with a pawn extra, and 6...Nxe4 7.Qd5 hits both the e4 knight and f7 with a strong initiative. Taking the center pawn is the most forcing and testing continuation.

Black's 6...Ng4 hits e5 and f2, but it's refuted tactically: 7.Bxf7+ Kxf7 8.Ng5+ forks the king and wins the loose knight on g4 with 9.Qxg4, leaving me a clean pawn up with Black's king stuck in the middle and castling rights gone. If Black declines with 7...Kf8 or 7...Ke7 I simply retreat the bishop and keep the extra pawn.

My bishop on f7 is hanging to Kxf7, so I must save it while keeping my two extra pawns — Bb3 retreats to safety and leaves Black's king stuck on e7 with his knight on g4 loose. I checked 8.Bg5+ Nf6 9.exf6+ gxf6, but then my f7-bishop is still lost and I only end up a pawn up, whereas after 8.Bb3 Ngxe5 9.Nxe5 Nxe5 10.0-0 I'm a clean pawn ahead with a far better position; 8...Nxf2 9.Kxf2 just drops a piece.

My e5 pawn is attacked three times (dxe5, Ncxe5, Ngxe5) and defended only once, so I should cash it in with check rather than let Black win it back — after exd6+ Black must answer the check, and only then do I play h3 to chase the g4 knight, keeping my two extra pawns. If instead I play h3 at once, Black equalizes material somewhat with Ngxe5, and note that Ncxe5 would lose a piece to hxg4.

I'm two clean pawns up, so I want to kick the annoying g4 knight and consolidate; 10.h3 works because after ...Nxf2 Kxf2 the follow-up ...Qxh2 fails to Rxh2 (the rook still guards h2), and ...Qg3 runs into hxg4 followed by Rf1/Rg1 trapping the queen's raid. After the knight retreats (10...Nf6) I simply castle and keep my extra material with Black's king stuck on e7.

After the queen trade I must recapture, and Bxd1 keeps my king able to castle while Kxd1 would strand my king in the centre and forfeit castling. Importantly, the h3 pawn already attacks the knight on g4, so after Bxd1 Black must spend a move saving it (Bxf2+ Kxf2 just loses material), leaving me two pawns up with a safe position.

The f2 knight forks my rook and bishop, so I need a move that attacks it while staying safe — Rh2 fails to 12...Ng4! 13.hxg4 Rxh2 since the h-file opens. Rf1 attacks the knight, keeps the h1 square covered (after ...Ng4 hxg4 Rxh1 Rxh1 I just win a piece), and after ...Nxd1 Kxd1 it's a plain trade leaving me a pawn up with an active rook on the open f-file.

Black's knight on d1 is simply trapped and undefended, so capturing it leaves me a full knight and a pawn ahead after all the queen trades. Kxd1 is safe — no black checks or forks follow, and I can then develop with Nd2/Be3 and consolidate.

I'm a pawn up with a safer structure, and I need to develop carefully — note that Be3 would simply lose a piece to Bxe3 since nothing recaptures. Bg5+ develops with tempo, forcing the black king to d7 or e8 before I consolidate with Nbd2 and Kc2.

I'm a clean pawn up and my pieces are active, so I want to improve them without conceding the bishop pair unnecessarily; Nd4 centralizes the knight, keeps the pressure of Bg5 on the pinned-ish Ne7, and even makes Be3 playable later. If Black takes with ...Bxd4, cxd4 gives me a strong center and leaves Black's knight still awkward, while ...Ng6 runs into Be3 since d4 now covers e3.

The key point is that 16.Rf7 defends e7 along the seventh rank, so after Bxe7+ the recapture Kxe7 becomes illegal — Black's knight is simply attacked twice and lost — while Rf7 simultaneously hits the undefended g7 pawn. Even the challenge 16...Rf8 fails to 17.Rxf8+ since no Black piece can recapture on f8 (the a8 rook is blocked by the king and the e7 knight doesn't cover f8).

After 17.Rxg7 the rook leaves f7 but now attacks e7 along the rank, so the knight on e7 is hit twice (Rg7 and Bg5) and defended only by the king. If Black grabs with 17...Bxd4 18.cxd4 the knight is still doubly attacked (18...Nf5 19.exf5), so I win material in every line while being a pawn up already.

Both my bishop (attacked by the h6 pawn) and my knight on d4 (attacked by Bc5) are hanging, so I need a move that solves both — 18.Be3 retreats the bishop to safety, defends the knight, and attacks the undefended bishop on c5. Captures like Bxh6 just lose material to Rxh6, and Bxe7+ or Rxe7 only simplify or lose the exchange; after Be3 Bxd4 Bxd4 I keep a dominant bishop, the rook on the seventh, and my two extra pawns, while 18...Rg8 19.Rxg8+ Nxg8 20.Bxc5 wins a whole piece.

I'm up two pawns with a sound position, so my priority is developing the queenside and bringing the king to safety rather than grabbing more material — Bxh6 just loses a piece to Rxh6, and Rg6 drops the rook to Nxg6. Nd2 develops the last knight (heading for c4 to hit d6), keeps the rook on g7 safe since nothing attacks it, and Bb4 ideas fail to cxb4.

Black's bishop on d6 is undefended, and Nf5 forks it together with the knight on e7, so Black's cleanest answer is Nxf5 exf5, which simplifies into an endgame where I keep two extra pawns and a dominant rook on the seventh. Other tries like Rg6, Bxh6, Rg8+ or Rxe7 all just drop material to the defenders (Nxg6, Rxh6, Rxg8, Bxe7).

Black's knight on f5 is attacking my rook on g7, so I must deal with it immediately; capturing with exf5 removes the attacker, and after Bxf5 the piece count is level (B+N vs two bishops) while I remain two clean pawns up with my rook still active on the seventh. Alternatives like Bxc5 or Bxh6 simply lose the rook to Nxg7.

My f5 pawn is actually hanging to Bd7 (via e6), so pushing f6 both saves it and creates a monster passer that Black's light-squared bishop can never touch. If Black hits the rook with Bf8 I retreat Rg6 where the rook supports f6; if Black tries Be5 to attack the pawn I answer Bd4 (backed by c3), and Rhf8 runs into f7! with Rg8 and promotion ideas.

My rook on g7 is attacked by Rg8, but Bxh6 solves that by both grabbing a free pawn (h6 is undefended) and defending the rook from h6 — if Black takes with Rxg7 I simply recapture Bxg7, keeping the f6 pawn supported and going three pawns up. Alternatives like Rg3/Rg6 just drop the rook, and f7 fails to Rxg7 followed by Rxf8.

Black's rook on g7 is completely undefended, and my f6 pawn backs up the g7 square, so Bxg7 simply wins a whole rook while keeping the dangerous f-pawn. If Black tries Rg8 to harass the bishop, f7 forks the rook and promotes; fxg7 instead would leave the pawn blockaded on g7.

Pushing the pawn to f7 is crushing: Black's Bd6 (or Be7) gets permanently tied to guarding f8, and 25...Rf8 loses the rook to 26.Bxf8 Bxf8 while the passer survives; 25...Be6 is met by 26.Rf1 defending the pawn and tripling the pressure on f8. If Black ever abandons f8 (e.g. 25...Bf4), 26.f8=Q Rxf8 27.Bxf8 wins a rook for the pawn.

My f7 pawn is one step from promoting and Black's rook on d8 can only meet it with Rxf8, which I recapture with the g7 bishop — netting a rook for a pawn and leaving me a rook and knight against two bishops with a healthy pawn edge. Bf6 also wins the rook, but Black can answer Rf8 and hold things together, so I prefer the forcing simplification.

Black just captured my new queen on f8, so the simplest and best reply is to recapture the bishop with Bxf8; after Rxf8 I'm left with knight and five pawns against bishop and three pawns, a clean two-pawn edge. Alternatives like Be5+ or Bd4 only let Black keep the bishop pair and activity.

My knight on d2 is pinned by the rook on d8 against my king on d1, which is why I have no knight moves, so unpinning is the priority; Bd6+ loses to Kxd6 and Bxc5 just loses the bishop to bxc5. Kc2 steps off the d-file, defends b2, and even if Black trades with Rxd2+ Kxd2 I'm a bishop and two pawns up with my dark-squared bishop controlling the h8 promotion square.

Black's bishop was eyeing my h3 pawn, so I push it out of reach with h4, keeping my extra piece and starting a dangerous passed pawn; Nf3 or Bd6+ would just drop material to Bxf3 or Rxd6, and Bxc5 trades my bishop for a mere pawn. Next I can harass the loose bishop with Rg1 while the h-pawn runs.

I'm up a knight and a pawn, so the cleanest plan is to run the h-pawn, which Black's lone bishop and rook can't realistically stop while my extra piece guards the queening path. Bxc5 would just trade my bishop for a pawn and reduce my winning margin, so I push h5.

My bishop on f8 is attacked by the rook on d8, so I need to address it; Be7 saves the bishop while attacking the rook with tempo (Rxd2+ Kxd2 would just hand me a rook for my knight). Bxc5 would only trade my extra bishop for a pawn, whereas after Be7 I keep piece for nothing and can roll the h-pawn.

My bishop on e7 is attacked by the rook, and Bd8/Bf8 both just lose it to Kxd8/Rxf8, while Bxc5 bxc5 throws away a piece for a pawn. Bf6 saves the bishop and crucially covers h8, so Black can never blockade my h-pawn with Rh8, keeping my extra knight and passer decisive.

My bishop on f6 is attacked by the rook, and I don't want to trade it off (Rf1 Rxf6 Rxf6 would throw away my extra piece), so I retreat it to d4 where it's safe and hits c5. This also keeps the plan of Rh1 next, hitting the undefended bishop on h3 while defending my h5 pawn.

Recapturing with cxd4 leaves me a clean two pawns up (a2, b2, d4, h5 versus a7, b6) with rook and knight against rook and bishop. Black's checks like Bf5+ are harmless since I can step aside or block with Ne4, and Re2 only hits a knight my king defends.

Black's bishop on g4 is hitting my h5 pawn, and Nf3 would simply drop the knight to Bxf3, while h6 allows Rxh6. Rh1 is the only move that defends the advanced h-pawn, keeps the rook on the file where the pawn wants to run, and after a check like Re2+ I just play Kc3 since both b2 and d2 stay covered.

I'm two pawns up with a dangerous h-pawn, and Rh4 attacks the undefended bishop on g4 while simultaneously supporting the pawn's march. If Black tries 36...Re4 to defend the bishop, 37.Nxe4 simply wins a rook, and after any bishop retreat (e.g. 36...Bf5+ 37.Kc3) I push h6-h7 with decisive effect.

Blocking on e4 loses material since e4 is attacked twice (Re6 and Bf5) but defended only once by Rh4, so the king must move; Kc3 is the most useful square because from c3 the king simultaneously guards d4, d2 and b2, killing Black's ideas of Re2 or Re4 hitting loose targets. The only annoyance is Re3+, after which Kc2 is safe and I keep my two extra pawns with the strong passed h-pawn.

My passed h-pawn is the trump card: 38.h6 is safe (Rxh6 is met by Rxh6 since my rook on h4 guards it) and threatens h7, when Bxh7 Rxh7 nets the bishop. If Black covers with 38...Bg6, then 39.Rg4 hits the bishop again, and even 39...Re4 40.Rxg6 leaves me a piece and a pawn up.
